title: The Prideful 5
content:
Wen Ning stood with his chin slightly dipped and arms hanging limp at his sides, motionless as a wooden puppet waiting for its puppet master to give the strings a tug.

His features were pale and delicately cut—even handsome in a brooding, melancholic way. But where his pupils should have been, there was only a stark, dead white. That pallor, coupled with the web of black, branching cracks creeping from beneath his collar up across his cheeks, twisted his sorrowful look into something deeply unsettling. The hem and sleeves of his long robes hung in shredded tatters, framing wrists as ghastly pale as his face, clamped in heavy black iron manacles with dangling chains. Thick shackles bound his ankles to match. That haunting metallic clatter had simply been the links dragging through the dirt with his every step. The second he halted, the mountain fell dead silent once more.

It wasn't hard to see why every cultivator on the ridge looked ready to drop dead from fright. Wei Wuxian was hardly faring any better; the shock crashing through his chest felt like a tidal wave swallowing him whole.

Wen Ning shouldn't have been anywhere near this mountain. In fact, he shouldn't have been walking this earth at all. Long before the siege on the Burial Mounds, his body should have been reduced to ash and scattered to the four winds!

Hearing someone scream that dreaded name, Jin Ling instinctively swung the tip of his sword away from the stone goddess. The Soul-Consuming Goddess seized on his lapse in focus, whipping out an elongated arm with sickening glee and hoisting him clean off the forest floor.

Seeing her maw stretch wide as she pulled Jin Ling toward her face, Wei Wuxian shoved his shock down and raised the crude bamboo flute to his lips again. His fingers trembled against the stops, spilling out an uneven, shaking cadence made even harsher by the rough craft of the hollow shoot. Two shrill, buzzing notes sliced through the gloom—and Wen Ning moved.

In the span of a single heartbeat, he crossed the clearing like a phantom, closing the distance instantly. He brought an open palm slashing down; with a sickening crunch of grinding rock, the Goddess’s body stayed fixed, but her stone neck snapped around in a complete circle. Her head now faced backward over her spine, that same vacant smile still carved into her lips. Wen Ning followed through with a bare-handed chop, severing the stone wrist clutching Jin Ling clean off the arm.

The Goddess glanced down at the neat, sheared stump of her wrist. Rather than twisting her head back around, her torso simply revolved a full hundred and eighty degrees, presenting her front and back to Wen Ning all at once. Wei Wuxian didn't dare drop his guard; sucking in a sharp breath, he focused on steering Wen Ning through the brawl. Yet with every passing second, a knot of unease tightened in his chest.

Low-tier walking corpses lacked the capacity for independent thought; they needed continuous spiritual nudges and explicit commands just to stumble forward. Even higher-tier fierce corpses were usually blinded by a haze of feral rage, devoid of any genuine intellect. Wen Ning, however, was in a league of his own. Handcrafted by Wei Wuxian’s own methods, he was indisputably the deadliest fierce corpse to ever walk the realm. Completely singular. He could think, reason, and make choices, unhindered by fear, fire, frost, poison, or any mortal frailty—virtually indistinguishable from the living.

Yet right now, Wen Ning showed not a single shred of personal consciousness!

Before Wei Wuxian could puzzle it out, gasps of awe rippled through the trees. Wen Ning had driven the Dancing Goddess into the dirt with a flurry of crushing blows, pinning her down before hoisting a boulder taller than a grown man above his head. He brought it slamming down onto her chest with bone-splintering fury. Blow after concussive blow hammered down like rolling thunder, pounding away relentlessly until the stone divinity was pulverized into a mound of pale rubble!

From the shattered debris rolled a smooth stone core, glowing with a soft, snowy radiance—the spiritual core formed after devouring the souls of nearly a dozen living cultivators. Handled properly, it could still restore the hollowed-out victims down in the village. But right now, not a single person spared a glance for the prize; every sword that had just been raised against the Goddess snapped around, leveling their steel directly at the fierce corpse.

One cultivator hollered at the top of his lungs, “Form a perimeter! Don't let him break through!”

A handful offered half-hearted shouts of agreement, but most hesitated, instinctively edging backward. The man shouted again, “Brothers, hold the line! Whatever you do, don't let him slip away—this is Wen Ning!”

That snapped them out of their daze. Slaying a rogue stone entity was petty change compared to the glory of bagging the Ghost General. Nobody had a clue how on earth he had clawed his way back from the grave, but capturing Wen Ning was worth more prestige than putting down a thousand soul-eaters! He was, after all, the Yiling Laozu’s premier lapdog—the silent, vicious hound that bit to kill without ever barking. Bringing him in meant instant, immortal fame across the great clans! Most of them had swarmed Dafan Mountain specifically to pad their credentials on dangerous game; hearing the stakes laid bare, plenty of swords began to itch. Yet the older, seasoned cultivators who had witnessed Wen Ning's blood-soaked rampages in their youth remained rooted to the spot, terrified to make a false move.

Seeing their reluctance, the man shouted louder: “What are you sweating for?! The Yiling Laozu isn't here!”

The crowd traded glances. He's right. What is there to fear? His master was hacked into mincemeat years ago!

Within seconds, the loose ring of hovering swords tightened around Wen Ning. Wen Ning swept his arms out, the heavy iron links whistling through the air in a brutal arc that knocked the airborne blades spinning off course. Lunging forward in the same breath, he clamped a hand around the throat of the nearest cultivator, hoisting the grown man off the dirt with zero effort. Wei Wuxian knew his earlier frantic notes had stoked the corpse’s dormant bloodlust; if he didn't reel him in now, it would turn into a bloodbath. Centering his breathing, he drifted into a completely different melody.

The tune floated into his mind on pure instinct—gentle, soothing, and serene, a world away from the screeching, erratic commands he’d been blasting earlier. The second the melody brushed his ears, Wen Ning froze. Slowly, his head turned toward the sound. Wei Wuxian held his ground, his eyes locking onto those blank, white expanses.

After a tense pause, Wen Ning loosened his grip, letting the breathless cultivator thud against the dirt. With his arms drooping at his sides, he shuffled step by step toward the flute.

His head sagged low, chains dragging through the fallen leaves, looking almost dejected. Wei Wuxian kept playing as he backed away, drawing the corpse deeper into the shadows of the timber. He had retreated only a short distance into the quiet woods when a crisp, clean scent of cold sandalwood brushed against his senses.

The next second, his shoulder blades bumped flush against a solid chest. A hand clamped down hard on his wrist, and the music cut out with a sharp choke. His stomach dropped. Whipping around, his eyes collided directly with a pair of pale, glass-clear eyes that burned with icy intensity.

Damn it. Lan Wangji had watched him command the dead with a flute countless times in their past life.

Lan Wangji kept an iron grip on his wrist, while Wen Ning stood barely two paces away, blinking vacantly into the trees as if searching for the melody that had suddenly vanished into thin air. Flickering torchlight and the shouts of the hunting party were creeping closer through the woods. Wei Wuxian’s thoughts raced, settling on a reckless gamble: So what if he’s seen it? Millions of people play the flute, and half the cultivation world tries to rip off the Yiling Laozu’s demonic tricks. Play dumb to the bitter end!

Ignoring the hand crushing his wrist, he raised his arm and brought the bamboo back to his lips. This time, the tempo was panicked and harsh, bordering on a scolding hiss—his breath hitching, the trailing notes screeching raggedly through the trees. Lan Wangji’s grip tightened instantly, squeezing so hard the bones in Wei Wuxian’s wrist felt seconds away from splintering. The searing pain forced his fingers open, and the crude bamboo flute tumbled into the dirt.

Fortunately, the parting command had come through loud and clear. Wen Ning wheeled around and slipped into the pitch-black timber, melting away without a sound. Fearing Lan Wangji would launch Bichen to cut the corpse down, Wei Wuxian instinctively lunged and grabbed the man’s sleeve. To his bewilderment, Lan Wangji hadn't spared Wen Ning a single glance; his pale eyes remained pinned entirely on Wei Wuxian.

They stood there in the dark, clutching at each other's wrists and robes, locked in a silent staring contest.

Right on cue, Jiang Cheng crashed through the undergrowth.

He had been nursing his temper down in Buddha's Foot Town, barely halfway through his first cup of tea, when an out-of-breath disciple came tumbling down the mountain, babbling about some terrifying monster tearing through the woods. Jiang Cheng’s heart had dropped into his boots, and he had sprinted up the slopes in a blind hurry, roaring, “A-Ling!”

Jin Ling had just narrowly escaped having his soul extracted, but he was standing on his own two feet now. “Uncle!”

Seeing the boy in one piece lifted a mountain off Jiang Cheng’s chest, which immediately converted into a blistering scolding: “Do you not carry signal flares on your belt?! You run into a beast like that and you don't even think to light the sky?! Who told you to play the hero? Get over here!”

Having let the Dancing Goddess slip through his fingers, Jin Ling was just as furious. “Weren't you the one who ordered me to bag it no matter what?! You told me not to show my face if I came back empty-handed!”

Jiang Cheng looked ready to slap the boy into next week, but since those words had indeed come out of his own mouth, he couldn't very well contradict himself. Turning his frustration onto the bruised cultivators picking themselves up around the clearing, he sneered, “And what kind of grand beast was it, exactly? Managed to mop the floor with the lot of you quite thoroughly.”

Tucked among the crowd in mismatched robes were several disguised Yunmeng Jiang disciples, planted by Jiang Cheng to quietly run interference for his nephew to ensure the kid walked away with the kill. One of the men was still staring blankly into the dark, his voice shaking: “S-Sect Leader… it was… it was Wen Ning…”

Jiang Cheng doubted his own ears. “What did you just say?”

“Wen Ning is back!” the man cried.

In a fraction of a second, shock, disgust, pure rage, and sheer disbelief collided across Jiang Cheng’s face.

It took several long, suffocating breaths before he squeezed out a voice colder than winter frost: “That creature’s bones were burned to dust and scattered for the whole world to see. How could he possibly return?”

The disciple stammered frantically, “It was him! It was really Wen Ning, I swear on my life! I couldn't mistake him!...” He whipped his arm around, jabbing a finger straight into the trees. “...He summoned him!”

Wei Wuxian was still tangled with Lan Wangji, and in an instant, every single eye in the woods swung toward them. Jiang Cheng’s sharp, lightning-cold stare tracked slowly across the clearing, locking dead onto him.

After an unbearable silence, a twisted, venomous smirk curled Jiang Cheng’s lips. His left thumb drifted unconsciously to the silver ring on his index finger, his voice dropping into a dangerous whisper: “...Well, well. You’re back?”

He uncurled his fist, and a long, crackling whip unfurled from his fingers, falling toward the dirt.

The whip was impossibly slender—a blazing ribbon of purple electric current humming with a vicious, spitting static, resembling a jagged bolt of azure lightning snatched right out of a storm cloud. Grasped firmly in his palm, a single flick could split the sky wide open.

Before Wei Wuxian could react, Lan Wangji’s seven-stringed guqin had already materialized in his hands. A single, sweeping stroke sent a shockwave rippling through the clearing, the zither's resonance clashing against the electric lash, neutralizing the blow mid-air.

Whatever sensible thoughts Jiang Cheng had harbored earlier about "avoiding unnecessary bloodshed" and "not antagonizing the Lan Clan" had been tossed out the window. Above the dark canopy of Dafan Mountain, flashes of violet lightning alternated with brilliant silver flares, thunderclaps drowning in the piercing, righteous hum of zither chords. The surrounding cultivators scrambled back to a safe distance, watching the spectacle with a blend of naked dread and rapt fascination. Opportunities to watch two peerless Clan Leaders trade blows were practically non-existent, and naturally, people were quietly hoping the brawl would get nastier. There was even a petty, unspoken thrill in the air—watching the delicate alliance between the Jiang and Lan clans shatter before their eyes promised endless entertainment.

Seizing the distraction, Wei Wuxian spun on his heel and ran for it.

The crowd gasped. The only reason that whip hadn't stripped the skin from his back was because Lan Wangji had been playing human shield. Bolting out into the open like that was practically begging for an early grave!

Sure enough, Jiang Cheng moved as though he had eyes in the back of his head. The second the runner cleared Lan Wangji’s protective shadow, Jiang Cheng seized the opening. With a vicious flick of his wrist, Zidian snaked through the air like a venomous dragon, catching Wei Wuxian dead center across the shoulder blades!

The impact sent Wei Wuxian tumbling forward, nearly vaulting headfirst into the timber. If the spotted donkey hadn't stepped into his path to cushion the blow, he would have cracked his skull open against an oak trunk.

Yet as the blow landed, both Lan Wangji and Jiang Cheng froze, staring in sheer bewilderment.

Wei Wuxian rubbed his aching lower back, bracing himself against the spotted donkey as he clambered up from the dirt. Safe behind the beast’s flanks, he practically yowled at the top of his lungs, "Oh, aren't you incredible! Big family, big power, tossing your weight around! Hitting innocent people whenever you feel like it! Tsk, tsk, tsk!"

Lan Wangji stayed dead silent.

Jiang Cheng’s jaw clenched, his mind racing between fury and disbelief. How is this possible?!

Zidian possessed a lethal, absolute trick: if a body-snatcher was struck by its lash, the soul and the stolen vessel were torn apart on impact. The possessing spirit would be ripped clean out of the stolen flesh, without exception. Yet this lunatic had taken a direct hit across the spine and was still jumping around, throwing tantrums like nothing happened. Barring the fact that this body wasn't possessed at all, there was simply no other explanation.

Behind the donkey, Wei Wuxian sneered to himself. Of course Zidian can't whip my soul out, genius. I didn't steal this body—it was handed to me on a silver platter. A forced sacrificial contract!

Seeing the sheer suspicion still darkening Jiang Cheng’s face, his hand itching to loose the whip a second time, Lan Jingyi piped up indignantly, "Sect Leader Jiang, that's enough! That was Zidian!"

Against a spiritual treasure of Zidian’s legendary standing, there was no such thing as failing on the first strike only to work on the second. If it didn't extract a soul, there was no soul to extract; if it didn't reveal a possession, then no possession had occurred. Anything else would mean Zidian was a complete sham. Calling it out like that backed Jiang Cheng straight into a corner, and given how viciously he guarded his own face, he couldn't very well lash out again.

Yet if this wasn't Wei Wuxian, who else in the world could command Wen Ning?!

Jiang Cheng refused to accept it. Leveling his crackling whip straight at the donkey, his voice turned venomously low. "Who the hell are you?!"

One of the nosy cultivators hovering on the sidelines cleared his throat, cautiously chiming in, "Ah, Sect Leader Jiang, you probably wouldn't bother with these kinds of petty rumors, but this Mo Xuanyu fellow... well, he used to be a disciple of the Lanling Jin Sect. An outer member, you know. But because his spiritual roots were weak and his progress stalled—on top of that business where he harassed a fellow male disciple—he was kicked out of Koi Tower in disgrace. Word is he completely lost his mind afterward. If you ask me, he likely turned to the crooked path out of bitter frustration when orthodox methods failed him. It doesn't necessarily mean... the Yiling Laozu stole his body."

Jiang Cheng snapped, "That business? What business?"

"Well... you know, that kind of thing..."

Someone else in the back couldn't resist blurting it out: "He prefers men! A cutsleeve!"

Jiang Cheng’s eyebrow gave a violent twitch, his disgust deepening with every syllable.

A few murmurs remained unspoken, though everyone was thinking them.

Terrible as his reputation was, no one could deny that before he defected from the Jiang Clan, the Yiling Laozu had been a strikingly handsome young gentleman—accomplished in the arts, effortlessly charming, officially ranked fourth among all the eligible young masters in the cultivation world. Coincidentally, this short-tempered Jiang Sect Leader had placed fifth, perpetually stuck in his shadow, which was why nobody dared bring up the old beauty charts to his face. Wei Ying had always been a shameless flirt, chasing pretty maidens and leaving broken hearts in his wake, but no one had ever heard a whisper of him having a taste for men. Even if he were to crawl back from hell... with Wei Ying’s haughty tastes, he would never have stooped to piloting a fruit-munching, donkey-riding, clown-painted lunatic!

Another cultivator muttered under his breath, "Honestly, it doesn't look like him at all... and that flute playing was downright atrocious. Talk about a cheap knockoff."

During the Sunshot Campaign, the Yiling Laozu had stood above the carnage, a lone bamboo flute echoing through the night as he steered armies of the dead to rip through enemy ranks like an unstoppable tide. His melody had been terrifying, majestic art; comparing that legend to the squeaking, dying-pig noises this discarded Jin bastard had just produced was an insult to the dead.

Wei Wuxian felt deeply victimized. You try going thirteen years without practice, hack a whistle out of a raw bamboo stalk with a stolen sword, and see what kind of masterpiece you manage to blow! If you can play anything that sounds remotely decent, I'll get down on my knees and kowtow to you!

A moment ago, Jiang Cheng had been utterly convinced he was staring at his greatest nemesis, his blood boiling hot. But Zidian had clearly delivered its verdict: Not him. The whip never lied, and it never failed. Forcing himself to calm down, Jiang Cheng ran the angles: It doesn't matter. I'll haul him back under any excuse, bleed him dry with every interrogation trick in the book, and see what spills out. He'll slip up eventually. It wasn't as though he hadn't done the exact same thing to countless suspected body-snatchers before.

Having settled on a plan, Jiang Cheng gave a subtle hand signal. Taking the cue, his purple-clad disciples fanned out to encircle the donkey. Wei Wuxian panicked, scrambling straight behind Lan Wangji’s white robes, clutching his chest with theatrical terror. "Ah! What are you trying to do to me?!"

Lan Wangji glanced back at him, enduring the obnoxious, overdramatic display without a word.

Seeing that Lan Wangji had no intention of stepping aside, Jiang Cheng’s voice chilled. "Second Young Master Lan, are you deliberately trying to cross me?"

Everyone in the cultivation world knew the young leader of the Jiang Clan was hopelessly paranoid when it came to Wei Wuxian. He operated on a policy of capturing ten innocent suspects rather than letting a single body-snatcher slip through; anyone who even vaguely resembled Wei Wuxian was hauled back to Lotus Pier for brutal torture. If this lunatic fell into his hands, he’d be lucky to leave with half his skin intact.

Lan Sizhui stepped forward, trying to mediate. "Sect Leader Jiang, the truth is plain to see. Young Master Mo hasn't stolen a body. Why must you torment a harmless, nameless wanderer?"

Jiang Cheng sneered, "Then I wonder why the esteemed Second Young Master Lan has gone out of his way to shield a harmless, nameless wanderer since the moment he arrived?"

A smothered snicker slipped past Wei Wuxian’s lips.

He poked his head out from behind Lan Wangji's back. "Sect Leader Jiang, look... your aggressive flirting is really putting me in an awkward spot."

Jiang Cheng’s brow jumped, a visceral gut instinct warning him that whatever was about to come out of this lunatic's mouth would be catastrophic for his blood pressure.

Wei Wuxian sighed with exaggerated pity. "I appreciate the passion, really, but you’re getting way ahead of yourself. Just because I like men doesn't mean I take anyone with a pulse. I don't just follow any guy who waves a finger at me. And frankly? You’re just not my type."

Wei Wuxian was deliberately gunning to disgust him. If there was one thing Jiang Cheng hated above all else, it was being told he was second best. No matter how absurd the comparison was, the moment someone claimed he fell short of someone else, he’d stew in bitter fury for days, refusing to rest until he proved them wrong.

Sure enough, Jiang Cheng’s face twisted into an ugly, mottled gray. "Oh? Then do enlighten me: what kind is your type?"

Wei Wuxian beamed. "My type? Hmm... Someone like Hanguang-jun. He’s totally my style."

Now, if there was one thing Lan Wangji despised above all else, it was shallow, shameless, frivolous banter. The moment the joke hit his ears, he would naturally recoil and put ten paces of distance between them to protect his pristine dignity.

Grossing out two birds with one stone—pure genius!

Yet, the moment the words left his mouth, Lan Wangji turned around.

His expression remained carved from pure, unreadable stone as he leveled a gaze at Wei Wuxian. "You said it yourself."

Wei Wuxian blinked, his grin freezing. "...Huh?"

Lan Wangji faced Jiang Cheng once more, his posture impeccably courteous, yet carrying an absolute, unyielding finality:

"This man is coming back to Gusu with me."

Wei Wuxian went rigid.

Wait, what?!
